translate_en|mods/HardshipBrawling/42/me: You knocked out %1. They look badly hurt.
%1 knocked you out for a moment.
%1 knocked you out for a moment. You're badly hurt.

Hold while aiming a gun to guard with it against melee hits. Unbound by default: the block key is the game's reload key. While aiming a gun this key only blocks; clicking drops the guard without shooting.

Hold with your fists up, or while aiming a melee weapon, to cover up against melee hits. While aiming a weapon this key only blocks (no sharpening). Clicking drops the guard without attacking; press again to block again. Held without aiming, with nothing that fights in your hand, Space with it is a kick.
Hold while running or sprinting to charge. Unbound by default: the charge uses the game's Melee key (Space) and replaces its shove while you run. On another key, the game's shove is left as it is.
Increases punch speed, damage and critical hits, and reduces the muscle strain, tiredness and hand injuries punching causes. Trained by landing punches.
Multiplier for the endurance blocking costs, held and per punch taken.

Hold the block key (Mod Options, R by default) with your fists up to cover up. You can't attack from a guard: clicking only drops it back to your stance. Your endurance only goes down while you block. Punches from the front land on your forearms for a fraction of the damage, less with Unarmed, never none. Each one costs a little endurance and leaves your arm sorer, and the one punching into it hurts their knuckles more; too many too fast, too little endurance or a sore or cracked arm breaks your guard. A broken arm can't punch or block.

Charging into a closed door that isn't locked and opens away from you shoulders it open without stopping, at no extra endurance. Locked, barricaded or blocked doors, and garage and sliding doors, stop the charge: you run into them, which costs what hitting someone does. A low gate (a fence you could hop) is shouldered open the same way; from its other side you vault it instead. Tall gates stop the charge.
Multiplier for the chance a weakened locked door bursts open on a kick. 0 = locked doors never burst open, they only break. Unlocked doors always swing open.
Multiplier for the damage a kick does to a door. Kicks never take a door below half its health.
Multiplier for the stiffness and pain kicking a door puts in the leg, and the chance of hurting the foot. 0 = none.

A guard kick (block + Space) at a closed wooden house door swings it open at once if it isn't locked and opens away from you. A locked one takes a long time: kicks do little damage, and once it is weakened every kick may burst it open, unlocked. Kicks never break a door: they wear it down to half its health at most. Use an axe for that. Strength and Unarmed hit harder. Every kick is loud and draws zombies, costs extra endurance and strains the kicking leg. Metal, security, glass, garage and double doors, tall gates and player-built doors can't be kicked in. A low gate (a fence you could hop) swings open with one kick if it opens away from you.
Multiplier for punch damage. Unarmed and Strength raise it.
Multiplier for the endurance each punch costs. Unarmed and Fitness lower it.
Landed punches make the punching hand sore and can scrape it. Unarmed and what you wear on your hands protect it.
Multiplier for punch damage on other players. The server's PvP melee damage setting doesn't apply to punches.
Multiplier for punch speed. Unarmed and Fitness make punches faster.
Multiplier for the muscle strain punching causes, mostly on the punching hand. Unarmed and Strength lower it. Also follows the game's Muscle Strain setting.
Fists with an item in hand
Aiming with a one-handed item in the main hand moves it to the other hand and raises your fists. Off: the item stays in the main hand and the fists only come up with an empty main hand.
Punching slowly wears out what you wear on your hands. Sturdier handwear lasts longer.
Fight with a gun in hand
Multiplier for pistol whip and butt stroke damage, on zombies and players.
Multiplier for the endurance a pistol whip or butt stroke costs. 0 = free.
How fast striking with a gun wears it. Maintenance, Blunt skills and Aiming slow it down. 0 = never.

Space while aiming a firearm strikes with it: a pistol whip or a butt stroke. Without aiming, Space is the usual shove. Blunt skills, Strength and Fitness count; strikes cost endurance and wear the gun.
With Casualties Undead installed, fists follow its body: missing arms can't punch, prosthetic arms hit softer, knockouts can cause concussions, and no fists while crawling, carrying someone or down.

With Hardship's medical mod installed (Hardship: Affliction), punches to the head add shock, and blows and kicks to the body a little. A couple of punches won't knock anyone out, but a real beating to the head can.
With Cye's Push Doors! installed, a door you charge open hits whoever is behind it with that mod's rules, and a door held shut by a crowd is forced open by it.
With The Only Cure installed, an amputated arm can't punch or guard (the other one still can), a prosthesis punches softer and takes no hand wear, and nothing lands on a limb that isn't there.
With Wound Expansion installed, an arm it disables (sling, dislocation) can't punch or guard, a nerve-damage fumble never drops the fists, and a knockout can leave a concussion.

Space while blocking (fists or any weapon) is a push kick. It hurts a little (it never kills a zombie on its own) and zombies may go down (more with Strength and Unarmed). Players are kicked low, in the stomach, groin or thighs, and may stagger (a kick to the groin always does, and a man feels it badly for a few seconds) or, less often than zombies, go down. A kick into a raised guard breaks it. It costs more endurance than a punch and the recovery is longer; Unarmed and Fitness make it a little faster. Not with a broken or deeply wounded leg, very stiff legs or very high pain. Not aiming, with nothing that fights in your hand, the block key + Space kicks too. Space otherwise is always the game's own shove.
Speed of a stealth knife kill from behind. 1 = vanilla.
Speed of a knife kill (the jaw stab) from the front. 1 = vanilla.
Speed of a knife stab at the ground. 1 = vanilla.
How long a knocked-out player stays on the ground, unable to act.
Punches to the face leave blood on that face and on the knuckles that threw them, or on whatever covers them. Higher values bloody faster; 0 turns it off.
For tuning: writes every punch on a player to the server console.
A forearm already hurt can crack while blocking punches, blunt weapons or axes with it, more often against higher Unarmed. Blades never crack it, and punches don't break arms otherwise.
A punch to the head or neck of a hurt player can stagger them, and knock them out when they're badly hurt.
A punch on a scratched body part can turn the scratch into a laceration, more often on the head.
Boxing, kickboxing and MMA gloves never take a player below 20 percent health; the punch that gets them there knocks them out. Below that, they can kill.
Multiplier for the endurance each tackle impact costs. Running itself costs what it always does.

Hold Space while running or sprinting to lower your shoulder and charge through whoever is in the way (it only counts once held a moment): a chance to knock them down and far less chance to trip. Fitness, Strength and Unarmed improve both; a heavy two-handed weapon hits harder but tires more. Not with a spear in hand. Off: Space while running is the game's own shove.
Multiplier for Unarmed XP, on top of the global XP multiplier.
Multiplier for how fast a weapon you block with loses condition. 0 = never.

Hold the block key while aiming a melee weapon (guns: their own key in Mod Options) to guard with it. Melee hits from the front lose most of their damage, less with your skill with that weapon; bullets are never blocked. One-handed guards leave your forearms and hands exposed (blades cut them); two-handed guards protect far better but wear the weapon. Blunt weapons and axes break guards faster; knives and spears get through them.
Years in a boxing gym and real fights against real people: fit, strong, and quick with the fists.
Grew up settling things with fists. Starts with some Unarmed and learns it faster.
